title: Probiotics in atopic dermatitis: A systematic literature review | Sędziak | Forum Dermatologicum
abstract:
#### Abstract  
**Background:** Atopic dermatitis (AD) is a chronic inflammatory skin disease characterized by eczematous lesions, pruritus, and impaired quality of life. Dysregulation of the gut–brain–skin (GBS) axis may contribute to AD pathophysiology, representing a potential therapeutic target. Probiotics have been studied for their immunomodulatory and microbiome-modulating effects.  
**Material and methods:** This systematic review was conducted according to PRISMA guidelines. PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science were searched for studies published between January 2005 and March 2025, using keywords “atopic dermatitis,” “probiotics,” “gut microbiome,” and “immunomodulation.” Randomized controlled trials (RCTs), systematic reviews, and meta-analyses were eligible. A total of 329 records were identified; 96 full texts were assessed for eligibility, and 32 studies were included. Extracted data included study design, population characteristics, probiotic strain(s), intervention duration, dosage, clinical outcomes \[SCORing Atopic Dermatitis (SCORAD), Eczema Area and Severity Index (EASI)], immunological parameters, and safety.
